content: The text provided appears to be a list of references from scientific and medical literature, specifically related to studies on antiviral therapies for hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection. 1. Antiviral therapy has been studied for patients with chronic hepatitis C and decompensated cirrhosis, as published in the Journal of Hepatology in 2016. 2. Chuang WL, Chien RN, Peng CY, and colleagues evaluated the efficacy of a fixed-dose combination of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir in Taiwanese patients with chronic genotype 1 hepatitis C virus infection, as reported in the Journal of Gastroenterology and Hepatology in 2016. 3. Conway B, Janczewska E, Luo Y, and others conducted the Malachite-I Phase 3B trial, comparing ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir, with or without ribavirin, to telaprevir plus peginterferon/ribavirin in treatment-naïve adults with HCV genotype 1. Results were presented in Gastroenterology. 4. Boker KH, Manns M, and Niederau C examined the real-world use, effectiveness, and safety of antiviral treatment in patients with chronic hepatitis C genotype 3 infection, as published in Alimentary Pharmacology and Therapeutics in 2017. 5. Curry M, O'Leary J, Brown RS, and colleagues demonstrated the clinical benefits of successful treatment in HCV-infected patients with decompensated cirrhosis treated with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir, as presented at the 22nd Annual International Congress of the International Liver Transplantation Society in 2016. 6. Curry MP, O'Leary JG, Bzowej N, and others evaluated the efficacy of sofosbuvir and velpatasvir in patients with decompensated cirrhosis, as published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2015. 7. Dashtseren B, Dendev B, Genden Z, and colleagues reported on the use of a single-tablet regimen of sofosbuvir/ledipasvir for hepatitis C treatment in Mongolia, as presented at the 26th Annual Conference of the Asian Pacific Association for the Study of the Liver in 2017. 8. Desnoyer A, Pospai D, Le MP, and others investigated the pharmacokinetics, safety, and efficacy of a full-dose sofosbuvir-based regimen in hemodialysis patients with chronic hepatitis C, as published in the Journal of Hepatology in 2016. 9. Deterding K, Honer zu Siederdissen C, Port K, and colleagues observed improvements in liver function parameters in patients with advanced HCV-associated liver cirrhosis treated with interferon-free antiviral therapies, as reported in Alimentary Pharmacology and Therapeutics in 2015. 10. Deterding K, Spinner CD, Schott E, and others conducted a Phase 2 study on the use of ledipasvir plus sofosbuvir for six weeks in patients with acute HCV genotype 1 monoinfection, as published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2017. 11. Dore GJ, Altice F, Litwin AH, and colleagues evaluated the efficacy of elbasvir-grazoprevir in treating HCV infection in individuals receiving opioid agonist therapy, as reported in the Annals of Internal Medicine in 2016. 12. Foster GR, Afdhal N, Roberts SK, and others assessed the efficacy of sofosbuvir and velpatasvir for HCV genotypes 2 and 3 infections, as published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2015. 13. Gane EJ, Hyland RH, An D, and colleagues studied the efficacy of ledipasvir plus sofosbuvir, with or without ribavirin, for 12 weeks in patients with HCV genotype 3 or 6 infection, as reported in Gastroenterology in 2017. 14. Hezode C, Colombo M, Bourliere M, and others conducted a Phase III study on the efficacy and safety of elbasvir/grazoprevir in patients with HCV infection and inherited blood disorders, as published in Hepatology in 2017. 15. Ide T, Eguchi Y, Harada M, and colleagues evaluated the efficacy and safety of direct-acting antiviral (DAA) therapy in a multicenter real-world cohort of chronic hepatitis C patients, as presented at the 67th Annual Meeting of the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases in 2016.
